title: Jinnah of Pakistan
author: Stanley Wolpert
current_text: Pakistan’s military dictator General Zia-ul-Haq banned Jinnah of Pakistan because it described Jinnah’s dietary habits, which author Stanley Wolpert had refused to remove. In 1989, Benazir and her government gave OUP permission to reprint Jinnah of Pakistan, and the book was released for sale in Pakistan.

sources.quote: Yet, Pakistan’s military dictator General Zia-ul-Haq banned the book, Jinnah of Pakistan, because there were lines in it describing Jinnah’s dietary habits, which Wolpert had refused to take out.
sources.title: The Genius of Stanley Wolpert – Newsweek Pakistan

sources.quote: In 1984, when wily Ziaul Haq ruled, came the finest biography of Jinnah so far written. Prof Stanley Wolpert's well-researched book, Jinnah of Pakistan, was published in the US by Oxford University Press and 500 copies were sent to Pakistan to be released for sale.
sources.title: `Bring back Jinnah`s Pakistan` - DAWN.COM

sources.quote: Thus the book effectively remained banned in Pakistan until in 1989, when, to give full credit to Benazir and her government, permission was given to OUP to reprint and the book was released for sale.
sources.title: `Bring back Jinnah`s Pakistan` - DAWN.COM

ban_rows.note: Banned in 1984 by the military dictator Zia-ul-Haq's government because of some 'offending passages'. Ban lifted in 1989 by the next democratic government.
